stories.new_fact: The Supreme Court heard argument on whether local governments can pursue state-court climate-cost suits against oil and gas companies.
stories.new_takeaway: Climate risk is becoming a venue, liability and public-budget question for cities, energy firms, insurers and bond buyers.
stories.why_now: The oral argument occurred on October 5, creating a new signal beyond the prior docket preview.
stories.previous_coverage: October 5 previewed the term and the climate case before argument; today's segment uses the argument as the new fact and shifts the takeaway to municipal finance and venue risk.
stories.uncertainty: The Court has not ruled, and argument signals can be misleading.
stories.watch: Watch for a ruling, procedural order, settlement movement or signal that similar city and county climate suits can or cannot proceed.

stories.new_fact: In-person absentee voting begins October 6 at the Franklin County Board of Elections at 1700 Morse Road, with week-one hours from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
stories.new_takeaway: The local election moves from registration deadline to live operations: lines, staffing, identification and mail-ballot handling.
stories.why_now: Early voting and absentee voting by mail begin today, October 6.
stories.previous_coverage: No recent episode covered the early-vote opening; prior Columbus segments focused on utilities, waterlines, transportation and local public-safety items.
stories.uncertainty: Hours are listed as subject to change, and actual line or mail performance is not known before voting opens.
stories.watch: Watch for reported line problems, ballot-mail delays, drop-box confusion, identification issues or changed hours.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac's October 5 Loan Selling Advisor release expands Best Efforts ARM Cash Contracts, intraday guarantor disclosure, wire-instruction improvements, data compare and import updates; the October 4 Income Calculator release adds written VOE and interested-party income support.
stories.new_takeaway: This is a secondary-market and income-documentation workflow change that can affect lock-desk execution, delivery discrepancy handling and rep-and-warranty support.
stories.why_now: The relevant Freddie technology changes took effect October 4 and October 5.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent home-lending segments covered Fannie pricing, FHFA bi-merge, Freddie Loan Closing Advisor OAuth, NFIP and rate movement; this uses a different Freddie delivery/income workflow.
stories.uncertainty: The release notes do not disclose lender defect rates, adoption or borrower cost impact.
stories.watch: Watch for seller notices, help-desk issues, ARM cash-contract adoption, income-calculator defects or delivery-data compare exceptions.

stories.new_fact: Upstart reported $1,378.3 million of September 2026 originations, $4,117.8 million for Q3, and an October 5 UMI of 1.49.
stories.new_takeaway: Production AI-lending scale needs to be interpreted separately from credit quality, because elevated macro risk can coexist with higher origination volume.
stories.why_now: Upstart published the September origination and latest UMI data on October 5.
stories.previous_coverage: No prior seven-day episode covered Upstart; recent bank AI segments covered Mastercard, Kyndryl/BIL, Barclays, Feedzai, Lead Bank and Bank of America.
stories.uncertainty: The release does not disclose approval-quality, loss-rate, fairness, partner-bank or manual-review comparisons tied to the AI model.
stories.watch: Watch for cohort losses, approval-rate lift, pricing accuracy, partner-bank performance or fair-lending review evidence.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added Upstart / consumer credit underwriting and marketplace pricing; new production row with company-claim evidence, disclosed origination dollars and UMI but no model-quality baseline.

stories.new_fact: OpenAI's pricing page says billing for gpt-rosalind-research begins October 5, 2026, with listed standard token prices and trusted-access limits.
stories.new_takeaway: Specialized frontier models are moving from lab announcement to priced workflow economics, but access limits and evidence rank still matter.
stories.why_now: The pricing effective date is October 5.
stories.previous_coverage: October 5 research listed GPT-Rosalind pricing as a candidate but the episode selected the federal AI task force instead; no full recent segment used this pricing angle.
stories.uncertainty: OpenAI's capability claims remain lab-and-partner reported; independent customer workflow replication remains limited.
stories.watch: Watch for independent life-sciences workflow evaluations, access expansion, price changes or customer evidence on cycle-time and experiment-quality effects.
stories.frontier_bar: Price/access shift for a specialized frontier model, with workflow implications.

stories.new_fact: AP reported the Dow rose 0.2 percent, the Nasdaq climbed 1.1 percent to a record, Brent settled a little over $100, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.31 percent.
stories.new_takeaway: Tech-led equity strength does not remove the borrowing-cost pressure facing mortgage desks, municipal borrowers and companies.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent market segments watched yields and oil; this is a compact fresh close with a record Nasdaq and higher 10-year yield.
stories.uncertainty: One session does not establish a trend; the next bond and oil moves matter more than the equity headline.
stories.watch: Watch whether the 10-year yield holds near 5.31 percent or moves lower enough to change mortgage and municipal-finance conditions.

stories.new_fact: NWS forecast for central Columbus calls for sunny weather, high near 67, southeast wind around 3 mph and no precipitation signal.
stories.new_takeaway: Weather should not disrupt commute, school, jobsite or errand plans; the useful adjustment is a morning layer.
stories.why_now: This is the current daily forecast for October 6.
stories.previous_coverage: Weather is covered daily only as compact planning information.
stories.uncertainty: Point forecasts update during the day.
stories.watch: Watch for any NWS forecast update that changes the dry-road and outdoor-planning assumption.

editorial_review.notes: Selected at least four fresh developments within 48 hours: Supreme Court climate argument, Franklin County early voting, Freddie Mac effective technology changes, Upstart originations/UMI, GPT-Rosalind pricing, and Monday market close. Compared facts and takeaways against the previous seven scripts; only the climate case is a continuation and uses the oral argument as a new fact with a different municipal-finance takeaway. Home lending leads with a specific operational workflow change rather than rates. AI in Banking adds a new ledger row. Frontier AI is a price/access shift, with older capability evidence labeled background.
